thesis: Amazon is in maximum-investment mode: Q1 2026 revenue $181.5B (+17% y/y) with AWS accelerating to +28% - its fastest growth in 15 quarters at a $150B run-rate - and Q2 guided above consensus at $194-199B with $20-24B operating income. The catch is the $200B 2026 capex commitment (the largest corporate capex plan ever), which crushes near-term free cash flow to fund AI infrastructure including its in-house chip line. The +6.5% week reflects AWS-acceleration optimism; the valuation question is when the capex wave converts back into FCF.
catalysts: Q2 2026 results July 31, 2026: guidance $194-199B revenue, $20-24B operating income (both above consensus)
AWS growth trajectory (+28% and accelerating; $150B annualized run-rate)
In-house silicon (Trainium) attach within AWS - the 'chip business inside AWS' narrative
Capex-to-FCF inflection signals: any sign the $200B peak-investment year normalizes in 2027
risk_factors: $200B capex in 2026 - FCF is deliberately sacrificed; if AI demand disappoints, the overbuild becomes writedowns and stranded depreciation
AWS competition (Microsoft, Google) in AI workloads; share shifts move the whole thesis
Antitrust/regulatory attention across retail and cloud
Retail margin cyclicality if the consumer weakens
At 31.2x trailing earnings the market already pays for the AWS acceleration continuing

aws_q1_2026_revenue.note: +28% y/y, fastest in 15 quarters; ~$150B annualized run-rate

fy2026_capex_plan.note: largest single-year corporate capex plan on record; near-term FCF challenged
